subject: Microburst latency, TTFT targets & streaming framing — follow-up
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novahealth.ai>, Anil Deshpande <anil@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Microburst latency, TTFT targets & streaming framing — follow-up

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear product use-cases you shared. I wanted to capture the performance/streaming items we discussed and propose concrete next steps for a short probe so we can validate TTFT and chunking behavior on our side. High-level recap: 

1) Goals (from your side) — confirm these align with what you said on the call:
- User-facing generation (short prompts, interactive UI) — target perceived snappiness.
- TTFT envelope: aggressive P50, conservative P99 targets (details below from Sofia).
- Streaming preference: SSE is preferred for your web clients; fallback to WebSocket if necessary.

2) Proposed SLOs to validate in probe (initial):
- TTFT P50 <= 150 ms, P95 <= 300 ms, P99 <= 600 ms for median prompt length (~30 tokens).
- Sustained throughput for pilot: 10 req/s average, with short microbursts to 50 req/s for <60s.
- Concurrency target: ~20 concurrent open streams per instance during peak UAT.

3) Streaming / chunk cadence considerations:
- Send an initial small chunk as soon as tokens are available (this improves perceived TTFT).
- Follow with 40–80 token chunks; cadence depends on model and tokenization (we'll measure approximate ms spacing).
- Heartbeat/keepalive: optional (we can do a lightweight newline heartbeat every 30s).

4) Operational asks for the probe:
- Can you confirm the sample prompt distribution (avg token lengths) and a small test corpus (CSV or JSON) we can use to simulate realistic traffic?
- Do you have any absolute P99 hard limits we should not cross for TTFT?
- Data residency: you mentioned US East as preferred region — confirm.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 2-week probe: first 3 days low-volume smoke, then ramp to the target throughput for 10 days, final 2 days for edge-case microbursts.
- Deliverables: SLO measurement report (P50/P95/P99 for TTFT and chunk cadence distribution), a short ops playbook for SSE fallback to WS, and a list of suggested model/quantization knobs if needed.

I attached an initial SLO proposal and a quick stream framing diagram for reference. If that plan looks good, can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to capture the test corpus and confirm API keys/access?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attach: slo-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)
attach: stream-framing-diagram.png (image)

From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novahealth.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Anil Deshpande <anil@novahealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Microburst latency, TTFT targets & streaming framing — follow-up

Thanks Ethan — great summary and thanks for the slide deck during the demo. Quick answers & clarifications from our end: 

- Confirmed region: US East (primary), with a secondary DR region in US West.
- Our target TTFT numbers (what product needs): P50 = 120 ms, P95 = 280 ms, P99 = 450 ms for the interactive flows. For batch/background workflows we have looser constraints.
- Streaming preference: SSE for web UI (we want event-stream simplicity). WS acceptable for mobile fallback. Heartbeat every 30s sounds fine; please include server-side idle timeouts in the notes.
- Chunk cadence we tried to capture: initial emit should be as small as possible (<= 40 tokens) and within the first ~50 ms for short prompts. Subsequent chunks: 50–80 tokens with target spacing around ~80–120 ms depending on model compute. Those are our ideal numbers — we expect some variability and want measurements during the probe.

Operational notes: 
- We can share a redacted test corpus (two CSV files: short_prompts.csv and mid_prompts.csv). I'll upload to the Drive link and share access by EOD.
- Compliance: we need Audit logs (token-level telemetry for the probe) and an initial SOC2 checklist — I attached our internal requirements doc for context.

If Redwood can consistently hit P95 <= 300 ms for this interactive template at the requested throughput/concurrency, we can move to an expanded pilot. For scheduling — tomorrow at 10:00 AM ET works for our engineering lead (Anil) and me.

Best,
Sofia Ruiz
Product Lead, NovaHealth
attach: nova_health_requirements.docx (docx)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Microburst latency, TTFT targets & streaming framing — follow-up

Quick internal note before the 10:00AM ET sync: 
- For the initial probe we should test two model configs in parallel: an FP16 baseline and an 8-bit quantized variant. Quant may improve batch throughput but might slightly increase TTFT variance — we'll measure both.
- I'll prepare a lightweight primer: cache priming for repeated prefixes (we can warm KV cache for their top-200 prompts) and a fallback policy that routes to a cheaper model if the primary is saturated.
- Ops ask: confirm whether NovaHealth will tolerate a short warmup phase where TTFT P95 may be higher for the first 1–2 hours while caches/VMs spin up. We should set expectations in the playbook.

Markus
Platform Performance Lead, Redwood Inference

Sofia / Anil — thanks for the targets and the drive upload note. Confirming next steps and immediate asks before tomorrow's call (10:00 AM ET):

1) NovaHealth to share: short_prompts.csv and mid_prompts.csv (redacted) + any traffic shape notes (we'll look at burst profiles).
2) We'll provision a small probe cluster in US East and run parallel configs (FP16, 8-bit quant) per Markus's plan. Expect a short warmup window; we'll capture warmup behavior explicitly in the report.
3) Our deliverables after the 2-week probe: detailed TTFT histograms (P50/P95/P99), chunk cadence timing samples, ops playbook (SSE->WS fallback), and recommended model/quantization profile.

I'll upload the SLO PDF and framing diagram to the shared Drive and include a HubSpot note after the meeting. If anything changes on your side please flag before 10AM ET.

See you tomorrow — calendar invite sent.

Ethan
